q: בת 75, דיירת במחלקה לתשושים הסובלת מדמנציה קלה ואירועי חרדה ברקע, מדווחת על דאגה מתמדת. הצוות המטפל בה מדווח כי היא מתקשה להתמקד ושהיא סובלת מנדודי שינה עם שיטוט מוגבר במהלך היום והלילה. היא השתתפה בטיפול קבוצתי במשך 6 השבועות האחרונים עם שיפור מינימלי. לא מטופלת תרופתית כרגע. מה הטיפול התרופתי המתאים למטופלת בקו הראשון?
o: Donepezil (Memorit)
Citralopam (Cipramil )
Oxazepam (Vaben)
Quetiapine (Seroquel)
explanation:
The vignette describes **anxiety symptoms in mild dementia**: persistent worry, difficulty concentrating, and insomnia, with minimal improvement after six weeks of group treatment. When medication is used for anxiety in an older adult, the source most strongly supports an **SSRI or SNRI** (Hazzard 8e, p. 1034).

**A. Donepezil (Memorit).** Wrong, donepezil treats Alzheimer disease symptoms; it is not the first-line anxiety medication described here, for which the source favors an SSRI or SNRI (pp. 912, 1034).
**B. Citalopram (Cipramil).** Correct, citalopram is an SSRI, a supported drug class for anxiety. Start cautiously and monitor adverse effects, including QT prolongation and hyponatremia (pp. 929, 1034).
**C. Oxazepam (Vaben).** Wrong, benzodiazepines can impair cognition, cause physiologic dependence, and increase falls. They are therefore not the preferred ongoing anxiety treatment in this patient with dementia (p. 1034).
**D. Quetiapine (Seroquel).** Wrong, an antipsychotic is not the preferred pharmacologic approach in the anxiety section; the persistent worry described here fits the SSRI/SNRI approach (p. 1034).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 912, 929, 1034.

q: A 78-year-old woman with age-related macular degeneration asks about supplements. According to the AREDS summary in Hazzard's nutrition chapter, which benefit was demonstrated in the original AREDS study?
o: Reduced first occurrence of AMD with an antioxidant and mineral combination
Reduced development of cataracts with an antioxidant and mineral combination
Reduced progression of AMD with an antioxidant and mineral combination
Reduced cardiovascular disease risk with the supplements tested in AREDS2
explanation:
**AREDS** distinguished slowing established AMD from preventing its first occurrence (p. 421). The study found "a slight reduction in progression (not prevention) of age-related macular degeneration (AMD)" with the specified combination of supplements (p. 421). The same discussion does not support cataract prevention and states that AREDS2 supplementation did not reduce cardiovascular risk (p. 421).

**A. Reduced first occurrence of AMD with an antioxidant and mineral combination.** Wrong, the reported benefit concerns progression rather than prevention of AMD onset (p. 421).
**B. Reduced development of cataracts with an antioxidant and mineral combination.** Wrong, the page states that there is no evidence that regular high-dose antioxidant and mineral supplementation prevents cataracts (p. 421).
**C. Reduced progression of AMD with an antioxidant and mineral combination.** Correct, slower AMD progression is the benefit attributed to the original AREDS combination (p. 421).
**D. Reduced cardiovascular disease risk with the supplements tested in AREDS2.** Wrong, the text explicitly states that AREDS2 supplementation did not reduce cardiovascular disease risk (p. 421).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 421.
ref: Hazzard Ch 30 — NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION
chapterTitle: NUTRITION DISORDERS, OBESITY , AND ENTERAL/PARENTERAL ALIMENTATION

q: האם ייפוי כוח מתמשך ניתן לביטול?
o: כן — הממנה יכול לבטלו בכל עת כל עוד הוא כשיר
לא; לאחר ההפקדה אצל האפוטרופוס הכללי אין לממנה אפשרות לבטל את המסמך
הביטול מותנה בצו של בית המשפט גם כאשר הממנה עדיין מבין בדבר וכשיר
האפוטרופוס הכללי מחליט על הביטול במקום הממנה גם כשהממנה עדיין כשיר
explanation:
**ביטול ייפוי כוח מתמשך** נעשה בהודעה בכתב למיופה הכוח, ויש למסור הודעה גם לאפוטרופוס הכללי. כאשר הממנה עדיין מבין בדבר, אין צורך להחליף את רצונו בהחלטה שיפוטית. הסייג שבסעיף 32כג(ד) עוסק בממנה שקבע במפורש שהמסמך יעמוד בתוקף גם אם יבקש לבטלו לאחר אובדן כשירות; במקרה זה ניתן לפנות לבית המשפט.
“ממנה רשאי למסור למיופה הכוח הודעה בכתב על ביטול ייפוי כוח מתמשך שנתן;” (סעיף 32כג(א), PDF עמ׳ 35).

**א. כן — הממנה יכול לבטלו בכל עת כל עוד הוא כשיר.** נכונה, הממנה הכשיר רשאי לבטל באמצעות הודעה בכתב למיופה הכוח; זהו ביטוי להמשך שליטתו במינוי (סעיף 32כג(א), עמ׳ 35).
**ב. לא; לאחר ההפקדה אצל האפוטרופוס הכללי אין לממנה אפשרות לבטל את המסמך.** שגויה, חובת ההודעה לאפוטרופוס הכללי אינה הופכת הפקדה למעשה בלתי ניתן לביטול (סעיף 32כג(א)–(ב), עמ׳ 35).
**ג. הביטול מותנה בצו של בית המשפט גם כאשר הממנה עדיין מבין בדבר וכשיר.** שגויה, המסלול הרגיל הוא הודעת הממנה. הפנייה לבית המשפט בסייג לאובדן כשירות אינה תנאי לביטול בידי ממנה כשיר (סעיף 32כג(א),(ד), עמ׳ 35).
**ד. האפוטרופוס הכללי מחליט על הביטול במקום הממנה גם כשהממנה עדיין כשיר.** שגויה, האפוטרופוס הכללי מקבל את הודעת הביטול; הסעיף מקנה את פעולת הביטול לממנה ולא מעביר את רצונו לפקיד (סעיף 32כג(א)–(ב), עמ׳ 35).

מקור: חוק הכשרות המשפטית והאפוטרופסות, סעיף 32כג, PDF עמ׳ 35.

q: An older man with urinary symptoms from benign prostatic enlargement reports improvement with tamsulosin. Which statement distinguishes symptom relief from prevention of urinary retention?
o: Symptom improvement shows that treatment reduces the risk of urinary retention
Alpha blockade improves symptoms but does not prevent urinary retention
Alpha blockade reduces prostate size through inhibition of androgen action
Symptom improvement indicates that treatment prevents dizziness and hypotension
explanation:
**Alpha blockers** relieve BPH-related urinary symptoms through effects that include reduced contractility of prostatic tissue, capsule, and urethra. This symptom benefit does not establish prevention of retention, and dizziness or hypotension remain possible adverse effects (p. 566).
"α-Blockers do not prevent urinary retention" (p. 566).
"decreased contractility of prostatic tissue, capsule, and urethra" (p. 566).

**A. Symptom improvement shows that treatment reduces the risk of urinary retention.** Wrong, the source explicitly states that alpha blockers do not prevent retention, despite their symptomatic benefit (p. 566).
**B. Alpha blockade improves symptoms but does not prevent urinary retention.** Correct, this distinguishes the reported symptom benefit from the absence of retention prevention (p. 566).
**C. Alpha blockade reduces prostate size through inhibition of androgen action.** Wrong, the source attributes prostate-size reduction through androgen conversion blockade to 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors, not to alpha blockers (p. 566).
**D. Symptom improvement indicates that treatment prevents dizziness and hypotension.** Wrong, dizziness and hypotension are adverse effects of alpha blockers, so improvement in urinary symptoms does not establish protection against them (p. 566).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 566.

q: A 77-year-old man with heart failure and multimorbidity has stabilized after hospitalization but continues to have symptoms and treatment burden. A palliative care consultation is being considered. Which description of its role matches Hazzard?
o: Improve quality of life and relieve symptoms alongside disease treatment
Replace disease treatment after determining that the illness is terminal
Defer symptom treatment until a decision is made to stop curative care
Shorten the remaining lifespan as the central purpose of supportive care
explanation:
**Palliative care** aims to improve quality of life and relieve the symptoms, pain and stress of serious illness. It is appropriate at any stage and can accompany curative treatment; it therefore need not wait for a terminal-stage decision (p. 1045).
"Palliative care aims to improve the quality of life for both the patient with serious illness and the family." (p. 1045).
"It is appropriate for any type of diagnosis, any stage of a serious illness, and importantly, can be provided together with curative treatment." (p. 1045).

**A. Improve quality of life and relieve symptoms alongside disease treatment.** Correct, this combines the stated aims of symptom relief and quality of life with the ability to continue disease-directed treatment (p. 1045).
**B. Replace disease treatment after determining that the illness is terminal.** Wrong, the source allows palliative care at any stage together with curative treatment, rather than defining it as replacement after a terminal diagnosis (p. 1045).
**C. Defer symptom treatment until a decision is made to stop curative care.** Wrong, symptom relief is a core purpose and is compatible with continued curative treatment (p. 1045).
**D. Shorten the remaining lifespan as the central purpose of supportive care.** Wrong, the described purpose is quality of life and relief of suffering; even hospice is stated not to aim at shortening or prolonging life (p. 1045).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 1045.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES
chapterTitle: PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: An older adult with chronic pain, cognitive impairment, and sedating medications asks about adding cannabis. Which safety consideration does Hazzard emphasize?
o: Cannabis may offset memory impairment caused by other medications
Cannabis may reduce the effects of concurrently used sedating substances
Cannabis may worsen memory impairment and contribute to medication interactions
Cannabis may reduce the adverse effects of the existing medication combination
explanation:
**Cannabis and medication review** are relevant when cognitive impairment is already present. Hazzard names cannabis among substances that can worsen memory impairment and notes that substances "can also interact with many medications, increase medication side effects, or lessen their efficacy" (p. 321).

**A. Cannabis may offset memory impairment caused by other medications.** Wrong, cannabis is named as a substance that can worsen memory impairment, rather than offset it (p. 321).
**B. Cannabis may reduce the effects of concurrently used sedating substances.** Wrong, the safety discussion raises concern about medication interactions and increased adverse effects; it does not identify counteraction of sedating drugs as a reason to add cannabis (p. 321).
**C. Cannabis may worsen memory impairment and contribute to medication interactions.** Correct, worsening memory impairment and potential medication interactions are the concerns described (p. 321).
**D. Cannabis may reduce the adverse effects of the existing medication combination.** Wrong, the source cautions that substances can increase medication side effects, rather than proposing cannabis to reduce them (p. 321).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 321.
ref: Hazzard Ch 23 — SUBSTANCE USE AND DISORDERS

q: An 86-year-old man receiving androgen deprivation therapy for advanced prostate cancer reports loss of libido. Which explanation connects the treatment goal with this sexual adverse effect?
o: Treatment raises available testosterone, which is associated with loss of libido
Treatment lowers available testosterone, which is associated with loss of libido
Treatment raises available testosterone, which is associated with increased libido
Treatment lowers available testosterone, which is associated with increased libido
explanation:
**Androgen deprivation therapy** lowers the testosterone available to stimulate prostate cancer growth. Hazzard describes severe testosterone deficiency during this treatment as being associated with loss of libido (pp. 550, 1416).
"treatment of prostate cancer with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) resulting in severe testosterone deficiency can be associated with loss of libido." (p. 550).
"The goal of ADT is to decrease the level of testosterone available to potentiate growth of the prostate cancer cells." (p. 1416).

**A. Treatment raises available testosterone, which is associated with loss of libido.** Wrong, the treatment goal is to decrease, not raise, available testosterone (p. 1416).
**B. Treatment lowers available testosterone, which is associated with loss of libido.** Correct, this combines the stated oncologic treatment goal with the described association between severe testosterone deficiency and loss of libido (pp. 550, 1416).
**C. Treatment raises available testosterone, which is associated with increased libido.** Wrong, it misstates the direction of testosterone change and the libido effect described in this setting (pp. 550, 1416).
**D. Treatment lowers available testosterone, which is associated with increased libido.** Wrong, the testosterone change is correct, but the source associates severe deficiency with loss rather than increase of libido (p. 550).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 550, 1416.
ref: Hazzard Ch 37 — SEXUALITY , SEXUAL FUNCTION, AND THE AGING MAN

q: An 85-year-old man hospitalized with pneumonia becomes disoriented, pulls at his oxygen cannula, and tries to leave bed after 36 hours without sleep. He is oriented to person only. Home medications are tamsulosin, metformin, and lisinopril. Temperature is 37.8 degrees C, pulse 92, blood pressure 135/80 mm Hg, respiratory rate 22, and oxygen saturation 91% on 2 L/min. His daughter says he would want everything done. Which initial supportive approach accompanies evaluation and treatment of his acute illness?
o: Use scheduled antipsychotic sedation to maintain bed rest during evaluation
Use a sitter and reorientation to support safe care during evaluation
Use benzodiazepine sedation to restore sleep during evaluation
Use wrist restraints to prevent movement during evaluation
explanation:
**Supervision and reorientation** are components of the initial nonpharmacologic management of delirium. Evaluation and treatment of contributors continue alongside these measures; medication may be needed if symptoms threaten essential care or safety, but the source recommends beginning with nonpharmacologic strategies (pp. 885, 888).
"The recommended management approach for all delirious patients begins with nonpharmacologic strategies" (p. 888).
"ensuring the presence of family members, use of sitters" (p. 888).

**A. Use scheduled antipsychotic sedation to maintain bed rest during evaluation.** Wrong, scheduled sedation for bed rest bypasses the initial nonpharmacologic approach, and sedatives can worsen delirium (p. 888).
**B. Use a sitter and reorientation to support safe care during evaluation.** Correct, sitters and repeated reorientation are explicitly recommended methods of supervision and communication (p. 888).
**C. Use benzodiazepine sedation to restore sleep during evaluation.** Wrong, benzodiazepines can worsen acute mental status changes and are not recommended as initial agents for delirium (p. 889).
**D. Use wrist restraints to prevent movement during evaluation.** Wrong, restraints reduce mobility and increase agitation, injury risk, and worsening delirium (p. 888).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 888, 889, 885.

q: בן 75, סובל מנפילות חוזרות. ברקע סוכרת ואוסטאוארתריטיס. מה מבין הבאים מנבא סיכון לנפילות עתידיות?
o: ערך צפיפות עצם T-SCORE של -2.7.
ירידה של 10 mmHg בלחץ הדם הסיסטולי במעבר בין שכיבה לעמידה.
זמן ביצוע Alternate Step Test מתוזמן ב-17 שניות להשלמת 8 צעדים
זמן ביצוע Timed Up & Go מתוזמן ב-10 שניות
explanation:
The **Alternate Step Test** assesses alternating placement of the feet on a step. Prolonged completion indicates impaired performance on a test with predictive accuracy for falls (p. 637).

**A. Bone-density T-score of −2.7.** Wrong, bone density assesses osteoporosis; this is not the balance and mobility measurement supporting the fall-risk inference here (pp. 771, 637).
**B. A 10 mmHg systolic fall on moving from supine to standing.** Wrong, this does not meet the systolic definition of orthostatic hypotension, which requires a fall of at least 20 mmHg (p. 667).
**C. Alternate Step Test taking 17 seconds for eight steps.** Correct, the table defines impaired performance as taking more than ten seconds for eight alternating steps; 17 seconds is therefore a concerning screen result (p. 637).
**D. Timed Up and Go taking ten seconds.** Wrong, the source recommends no cutoff for predicting community falls, so ten seconds is not the clearest predictive finding among these options (p. 637).

TUG has limited predictive value for falls in community-dwelling older adults, with no recommended cutoff (p. 637).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 637, 667, 771.

q: An 85-year-old woman with advanced COPD and a rib fracture after a fall is undergoing respiratory monitoring. Which feature of her underlying lung disease represents a preexisting physiologic impairment?
o: Airway dilation and increased gas exchange surface area
Airflow obstruction and air trapping within the lungs
Increased elastic recoil and improved airflow through airways
Alveolar regeneration and improved gas exchange within the lungs
explanation:
**COPD** involves airflow obstruction, air trapping, hyperinflation, and gas exchange abnormalities. Airway and alveolar structural changes obstruct airflow, while emphysematous destruction reduces alveolar attachments and elastic recoil (p. 1240). "Other key physiologic impairments include air trapping and hyperinflation and gas exchange abnormalities." (p. 1240).

**A. Airway dilation and increased gas exchange surface area.** Wrong, the source describes obstruction and progressive loss of gas exchange surface area, rather than expansion of that surface (p. 1240).
**B. Airflow obstruction and air trapping within the lungs.** Correct, airflow obstruction and air trapping are explicitly described physiologic impairments of COPD (p. 1240).
**C. Increased elastic recoil and improved airflow through airways.** Wrong, emphysematous alveolar destruction decreases elastic recoil and contributes to obstruction, rather than improving airflow (p. 1240).
**D. Alveolar regeneration and improved gas exchange within the lungs.** Wrong, the source describes enhanced cell death and inadequate regeneration associated with progressive loss of gas exchange surface area (p. 1240).

Source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 1240.
ref: Hazzard Ch 81 — CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE

q: בת 82 התקבלה לשיקום לאחר ניתוח החלפה מלאה של מפרק ירך ימין בעקבות שבר אוסטאופורוטי. ברקע: מחלה ריאתית חסימתית כרונית, אי ספיקה לבבית כרונית עם מקטע פליטה 55%, יתר לחץ דם, סוכרת, השמנת יתר. בבדיקות מעבדה שנלקחו לבירור מעבדתי של אנמיה נצפו התוצאות הבאות: TSH = 40 mlU/L (נורמה 0.35-4.5), FT4 = 8 pmol/L (נורמה 10-20). כמו כן מדווחת על עצירות, חולשה כללית, וירידה בזיכרון לטווח קצר. מהי הגישה הטיפולית המתאימה?
o: התחלת טיפול ב- LEVOTHYROXINE (ELTROXIN) במינון 100 מק''ג ליממה
ממצא אופייני לאחר שבר בצוואר הירך, לא מצריך טיפול, מומלץ לחזור על הבדיקה לאחר השיקום
התחלת טיפול ב- LEVOTHYROXINE (ELTROXIN) ובדיקת מעקב חוזרת לאחר שבועיים
התחלת טיפול ב- LEVOTHYROXINE (ELTROXIN) עם יעד TSH של 4-6 mlU/L
explanation:
In this older patient with **hypothyroidism**, high TSH and low free T4 call for levothyroxine. The source permits a higher TSH target in older age and emphasizes avoiding overreplacement because of atrial fibrillation and bone-loss risks (p. 1552).

**A. Start levothyroxine (Eltroxin) at 100 micrograms daily.** Wrong, for an older patient with cardiac disease, the source recommends starting low and increasing slowly; 25 or 50 micrograms are described as reasonable starting doses. Thus 100 micrograms is not the appropriate starting dose here (p. 1552).
**B. This is typical after hip fracture; defer treatment and repeat testing after rehabilitation.** Wrong, the stem describes high TSH with low free T4 and symptoms, not merely a mild abnormality without hormone deficiency. Inference from these findings and treatment principles: the fracture alone does not justify deferring treatment until rehabilitation ends (p. 1552).
**C. Start levothyroxine and repeat testing after two weeks.** Wrong, TSH testing for dose adjustment usually occurs after six weeks; older patients may need seven to eight weeks to reach steady state because of slower clearance. Two weeks does not match the monitoring interval described for titration (p. 1552).
**D. Start levothyroxine with a TSH target of 4–6 mIU/L.** Correct, the source permits this target above age 80. Age-adjusted targeting reduces overreplacement risk, relevant to cardiac disease and an osteoporotic fracture (p. 1552).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 1552.

q: What incidence of new-onset constipation was found in nursing home residents screened every 3 months?
explanation:
Nursing-home residents screened every three months had a 7% incidence of new-onset constipation (p1355).

B. 37%: This is failure to expel a test sphere in non-constipated older subjects (p1357); the requested value is 7% (p1355).
D. 14%: This is the proportion with elicitable rectal contractions among older people with prior rectal impaction (p1357); the requested value is 7% (p1355).
A. 13%: This is constipation in the calcium-supplement treatment group of a five-year study (p1359); the requested value is 7% (p1355).
retiredReason: Number recall from one passage; not exam-style.

q: In older adults, what is a key pitfall in recognizing infectious back pain (eg, discitis/osteomyelitis)?
o: Endovascular infection risk generally favors a mechanical explanation for the presenting back pain
Disc infection generally differs sufficiently from mechanical disease to permit straightforward clinical recognition
Fever is sometimes absent despite the presence of spinal infection in older adults
Fever is generally required before spinal infection should enter the differential for back pain
explanation:
**Spinal infection without fever** is an important recognition pitfall in older adults. Disc involvement can produce signs and symptoms resembling mechanical disease, and endovascular-infection risk should heighten suspicion for an infectious cause rather than reassure the clinician (p. 1631).
"fever can be absent in older patients with infection." (p. 1631).

**A. Endovascular infection risk generally favors a mechanical explanation for the presenting back pain.** Wrong, endovascular-infection risk should alert the clinician to an infectious cause of back pain, not favor a mechanical attribution (p. 1631).
**B. Disc infection generally differs sufficiently from mechanical disease to permit straightforward clinical recognition.** Wrong, disc involvement can mimic mechanical disc disease, so clinical resemblance does not reliably separate the two (p. 1631).
**C. Fever is sometimes absent despite the presence of spinal infection in older adults.** Correct, the source explicitly notes that older patients with infection may lack fever, so an afebrile presentation does not exclude spinal infection (p. 1631).
**D. Fever is generally required before spinal infection should enter the differential for back pain.** Wrong, requiring fever would miss the afebrile infections described in older patients (p. 1631; inference).

Source: Hazzard's Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 1631.

q: What serum lactate cutoff predicts 30-day mortality in older adults with pneumonia?
o: No serum lactate cutoff is described
Any lactate value, without a threshold
Below 2 mmol/L
At least 2 mmol/L
explanation:
**Serum lactate is a prognostic marker** in older adults with pneumonia (p. 1685). This matters in a setting where impaired inflammatory responses can cause routine inflammatory measurements to underestimate illness severity; “Serum lactate value greater than or equal to 2 mmol/L is a predictor of 30-day mortality in older adults.” (p. 1685).

**A. No serum lactate cutoff is described.** Wrong, the source explicitly identifies a lactate cutoff, so denying any threshold discards the stated prognostic finding (p. 1685).
**B. Any lactate value, without a threshold.** Wrong, the reported association is tied to a defined threshold; the page does not present every lactate value as the same risk marker (p. 1685).
**C. Below 2 mmol/L.** Wrong, values below this boundary do not meet the stated predictor; that does not prove an individual patient has no mortality risk (inference from p. 1685).
**D. At least 2 mmol/L.** Correct, this value meets the threshold associated with the specified mortality outcome in older adults (p. 1685).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 1685.
